title: DroneClear
question: How does a drone fly?
hook: A drone has no tilting blades and no gearbox, yet it hovers, climbs and turns on the spot. It does it by changing four propellers' speeds up to hundreds of times a second.

explainer.title: The one-line idea
explainer.text: A quadcopter moves by changing how fast four propellers spin. Speed up one side and it tips; speed up two diagonal propellers and it turns.

explainer.title: The part people get wrong
explainer.text: A drone does not stay level by magic. A feedback loop measures the tilt hundreds of times a second, and a PID controller decides how hard to push back.

explainer.title: Keeping level
explainer.text: The P, I and D dials set how hard, how long and how smoothly the drone corrects. Too much P makes it wobble; too little lets it sag.

explainer.title: Moving
explainer.text: Lean to fly forward, speed all four to climb, and speed one diagonal pair to turn. The rotors never tilt.

explainer.title: The battery
explainer.text: Watt-hours against hover power set the flight time, and every extra gram of payload costs minutes.

explainer.title: The rules and the uses
explainer.text: India's Drone Rules, 2021 set green, yellow and red airspace and register drones on Digital Sky. Drones map, spray and deliver under official schemes.

concepts.def: A drone with four motors and propellers, two spinning clockwise and two anticlockwise.
An electronic switch that sets how fast one motor turns by chopping the battery's power.
A sensor that measures how fast the drone is turning around each axis.
A feedback rule that combines a proportional push, an integral correction and a derivative brake.
Total rotor push minus the drone's weight; only this part changes its height.
A unit of energy: one watt for one hour, equal to volts times amp-hours.
The drone plus its battery and payload, which decides its class under the Drone Rules.
The DGCA's online platform for drone registration and the official airspace map.
